strings.ah_ai: **The AI:** inside Claude the assistant is Claude itself, a real AI model that sees your screen and numbers and can fill in fields. On the website you can connect a free Gemini key in Settings. Without one, the app's own personal model answers, offline too.
strings.ah_design: **Design and theme:** Settings → Display and language → Look. Pick one of 14 designs and a color theme there. Quicker: the palette button at the top. A theme colors any design; "By device" brings back the design's own colors.
strings.ah_hol: **Holiday effects:** holiday themes come with effects such as flags and fireworks, snow and lanterns. Turn them off in Settings → Display and language → Look → Holiday effects. Automatic switching to the holiday theme can be turned on there too.
strings.ah_lang: **Language, currency and country:** Settings → Display and language → Language and region. Choose the interface language, display currency and country of origin there; picking a country also offers its currency. The עב / عر / EN buttons at the top switch language too.
strings.ah_live: **Live data:** rates update in real time. Turn them off with the "Live updates" switch on Home, or search "market data" in Settings. With them off you see the previous trading day's closing rate, with its date. The round arrow at the top refreshes everything.
strings.ah_pdf: **Share and PDF:** under the result on every calculator there are Copy, Share and PDF buttons. Saved files can also be downloaded or shared from the Saved folder.
strings.ah_reset: **Clearing and reset:** the round arrow at the top of a calculator resets that screen. "Clear all" in the save bar deletes what was saved. Single files are deleted in the Saved folder. To reset the whole app: Settings → System → Data and reset.
strings.ah_saved: **Saved:** every save makes a file in the Saved folder (the bookmark icon). Each file can be opened, downloaded, shared or deleted at once. With automatic saving each calculator keeps one file that updates itself.
strings.ah_sep: **Separators:** Settings → Display and language → Numbers. Choose the thousands separator (comma, dot, space, apostrophe or none) and whether to group digits while you type.
strings.ah_what: **What's in the app:** dozens of financial calculators for Israel: salary and the full payslip, tax, mortgage and loans, savings and compound interest, pension, investments, currencies and live rates, real estate and more. There's also a Saved folder, sharing and PDF, 14 designs, holiday themes, three languages and this assistant. Tap a calculator on Home, or ask me which one fits you.

{to}Hello,

On {d} I bought {p} from you. The product is still under warranty (until {e}), and it has stopped working properly: [describe the fault briefly].

Thank you,
[your name]

strings.gl_d_annfac: The number your pension balance is divided by to get the monthly pension. Lower factor = higher pension.
strings.gl_d_balloon: A mortgage where you pay only interest during the term and the principal at the end.
strings.gl_d_bond: A loan to a government or company that pays interest. Usually less volatile than stocks.
strings.gl_d_compound: Interest earned on interest already added. Over years it's what makes savings grow fast.
strings.gl_d_cpi: A monthly CBS index measuring price changes in a basket of goods and services.
strings.gl_d_cpitrack: A mortgage track whose balance rises with CPI. Low starting payment that grows with inflation.
strings.gl_d_dd: Permission for a company to charge your account monthly. Review them now and then.
strings.gl_d_dti: The share of income going to the mortgage payment. Banks cap it; around a third is usually advised.
strings.gl_d_etf: A fund tracking an index like TA-125 or the S&P 500. Broad spread with low fees.
strings.gl_d_exempt: Self-employed with low turnover who doesn't charge VAT. Above a yearly cap you become licensed.
strings.gl_d_f106: Your employer's yearly summary of pay and tax withheld. Needed for a refund.
strings.gl_d_f161: Filled by the employer when a job ends, to set the tax on severance.
strings.gl_d_fees: The fee a savings fund charges on deposits and balance. A small difference adds up to a lot over years.
strings.gl_d_gemel: Long-term retirement savings. An investment provident fund can be withdrawn anytime (with tax on gains).
strings.gl_d_grant: A tax-authority grant for low-income workers and self-employed. You apply each year.
strings.gl_d_gross: Pay before any deductions – tax, National Insurance and pension.
strings.gl_d_hish: Medium-term savings with a tax break: liquid after 6 years, gains tax-free up to a cap.
strings.gl_d_infl: A general rise in prices. Money that earns less than inflation loses buying power.
strings.gl_d_landtax: Tax on the profit from selling property. A single home is usually exempt, with conditions.
strings.gl_d_lease: Renting a car long-term for a monthly fee. It isn't yours at the end unless you buy it.
strings.gl_d_licensed: Self-employed who charges VAT, pays it on, and deducts VAT on expenses.
strings.gl_d_link: A linked amount moves with prices – like a linked mortgage or rent.
strings.gl_d_ltv: The percent of the home's value the mortgage covers. Capped at 75% for a single home.
strings.gl_d_marginal: The tax rate on your next shekel. It's higher than your average rate.
strings.gl_d_net: What actually reaches your account after all deductions.
strings.gl_d_ni: A compulsory payment funding benefits like unemployment, maternity and old age, plus health insurance.
strings.gl_d_nurs: Pays when someone needs ongoing help with daily activities, usually in old age.
strings.gl_d_od: A negative bank balance. It's an expensive loan with high interest.
strings.gl_d_pensfix: A request to the tax authority at retirement setting how much pension and grants are tax-free. Worth filing.
strings.gl_d_point: A fixed amount that cuts income tax. Every resident has points; more for women, parents, discharged soldiers and others.
strings.gl_d_polsav: Savings through an insurer, withdrawable anytime. Tax is only on the real gain.
strings.gl_d_prepay: A fee a bank may charge when you repay early, mainly on fixed-rate tracks.
strings.gl_d_prime: Banks' base rate: the Bank of Israel rate plus 1.5%. Many loans and mortgage tracks follow it.
strings.gl_d_purch: Tax the buyer pays on property. A single home has a tax-free bracket.
strings.gl_d_refund: Money returned when you overpaid – e.g. after changing jobs or unused credits.
strings.gl_d_sev: Money due to a dismissed worker after at least a year – usually a month's pay per year.
strings.gl_d_shaban: A health fund's extra plan beyond the basic basket. Usually fairly cheap.
strings.gl_d_stock: A small share of a company. It can rise or fall a lot short-term.
strings.gl_d_var: A rate that resets during the loan – every 5 years or with prime.
strings.gl_d_yield: How much an investment gained or lost, in percent, over a period.
strings.gl_intro: Money terms in plain words. Jump from each term to its calculator.
strings.gpt_intro: You can also develop the app with ChatGPT: it connects to the GitHub repository, changes the code, and after you approve, the website and app update by themselves.
strings.gpt_s1: In ChatGPT: Settings → Connectors → GitHub, and sign in with your account.
strings.gpt_s2: Give access to the financial-calculator repository only.
strings.gpt_s3: Open Codex and ask for a change. The code is in the src folder and the build steps are in AGENTS.md.
strings.gpt_s4: Approve the change (Merge) – within minutes the site is rebuilt and published.
strings.gpt_safe: Only someone with access to the GitHub repository can change the code. Visitors to the site or app cannot.
strings.gr_diffS: a month, vs full-time until retirement
strings.gr_intro: Fewer hours in the last years means smaller pension deposits. Here you see how much that lowers the pension.
strings.gr_note: You can ask the employer to keep pension deposits at the full salary – worth asking.
strings.gs_none: Not found in calculators or settings. You can ask the assistant.
strings.gs_ph: A calculator, term or setting: mortgage, credit points, reserve…
strings.gs_tip: Tip: open search from anywhere with / or Ctrl+K.
strings.h_acDepRate: A shekel deposit renewed each year, 15% tax on the profit.
strings.h_acLoanBal: 0 if there is no loan. Anything above the balance, and the monthly addition, go to the deposit.
strings.h_acMktRet: Your assumption, not a promise. The market can also fall, especially over a short time. 25% tax on the real gain.
strings.h_acMon: Monthly saving or investing with regular deposits. 0 if none.
strings.h_account: Sign-up: a unique username (@) and a strong password. The username is checked against everyone using the app inside claude.ai, so no two are the same. The password and your data are stored encrypted on this device only, so another device needs its own sign-up. Forgot the password? It cannot be recovered, because it is not stored anywhere.
strings.h_aiEngine: The personal model always works, even offline, and explains terms, calculators and results. Gemini also handles open questions.
strings.h_aiNet: When the assistant doesn't know, it looks the question up on Wikipedia and uses the app's live data. Only the question is sent. Without it, it answers from built-in knowledge only.
strings.h_aiWho: Calculations, rates, indices and built-in definitions are always answered at once, exactly, inside the app. Any other question opens in the service you choose, with no account, together with this screen's numbers. The question is also copied in case the service doesn't fill it in.
strings.h_apSb: Watts during the hours it is off but plugged in
strings.h_apTar: Home tariff from July 2026: 0.6352 ₪ incl. VAT
strings.h_autoRef: Checks the daily rate source as a backup to live rates.
strings.h_beTax: When set, the profit target is after tax
strings.h_bench: The index's average yearly return over the last 10 years, without dividends.
strings.h_benefit: For example a company car. Added to the tax and National Insurance base
strings.h_blankKeep: Leave empty to keep each calculator's own value
strings.h_bnW6: Gross pay insured with National Insurance
strings.h_bnWk: Full after 10 months of work out of 14
strings.h_boiDb: Updates every business day after 16:00 and reaches open pages instantly. Available when signed in to claude.ai.
strings.h_cSpread: How many points below (cautious) or above (hopeful) the return you entered. These are assumptions, not a forecast.
strings.h_capInc: Dividends, interest and gains. Counted here only for the surtax
strings.h_cbPay: What you pay the employer for the car
strings.h_cbPrice: The price when the car was new
strings.h_ccExtra: See how a small extra shortens the debt and saves interest
strings.h_cl: Add your current plan or an offer you got – it is compared with all plans.
strings.h_cl2: Pick a company or "Other" and type a name (✏️ to rename). A copied plan can be changed – price, GB, promo – and joins the comparison.
strings.h_clDueDay: The default is the 15th. Change it to whatever applies to your clients.
strings.h_clMonths: Average price over the period – including the rise after the promo.
strings.h_clNow: All lines together – to see the saving.
strings.h_clockHeb: The Hebrew date changes at midnight, not at sunset.
strings.h_connAll: No account, no key, no sign-up. Every source here is open and connects automatically.
strings.h_country: Kept only on your device. Gives the AI context and suggests that country's currency.
strings.h_cpiCap: The inflationary part is exempt; tax applies to the real gain. Enter 0 to ignore
strings.h_crFill: The first time, the amounts come from your portfolio.
strings.h_crRet: An assumption – for the time to come back.
strings.h_custom: 1 source = ? target. Leave empty to use the current rate.
strings.h_cvLive: Dollar, euro and crypto update from Coinbase when the page can reach the server. Inside claude.ai: the Bank of Israel official rate, updated each business day.
strings.h_daFee: The commission is part of the cost, so of the average too
strings.h_daTgt: How many units to buy at the purchase price to reach this average. 0 = skip
strings.h_dealer: Enter revenue and expenses before VAT
strings.h_design: A design sets the style: cards, buttons, images and effects. The theme sets the colors, in every design. "By device" keeps the design's own colors.
strings.h_dkAdd: Optional. Goes in at the start of each month, from the second month.
strings.h_dkChg: For example −0.25 if a cut is expected. This is your assumption, not a forecast.
strings.h_dkComp: Interest added to the principal earns interest itself – compound interest. "At the end" is simple interest.
strings.h_dkCpi: Used for the real value, and in a CPI-linked deposit for the linkage too. This is an assumption.
strings.h_dkCut: In some deposits leaving at an exit point pays a lower rate. 0 if not.
strings.h_dkExit: You can leave only at an exit point. A number that is not one is rounded down to the one before.
strings.h_dkFx: Positive – the currency gains against the shekel. An assumption only; exchange rates swing.
strings.h_dkKind: Fixed: the rate is known up front. Variable: moves with prime. CPI-linked: the principal rises with the index, plus interest. Currency-linked: in dollars or euros, exposed to the exchange rate. Exit points: you can leave on set dates. Renewing: available every day, week or month. Structured: the return follows a stock index.
strings.h_dkRate: Shekel, variable and renewing: the rate the bank offers. CPI-linked: the rate above the index. Currency-linked: the rate in that currency.
strings.h_dkStruct: The return depends on the index, so it is not known up front. The principal is usually protected, but you may get only the minimum.
strings.h_dlMonths: Money not yet invested stays in cash.
strings.h_dlVol: A broad share index is about 15%–20%. Crypto – much more.
strings.h_donation: 35% credit, up to 30% of income. A yearly minimum applies
strings.h_dpExtra: Goes to the target debt and grows as debts are cleared.
strings.h_ecEeS: Usually 2.5% when the employer puts in 7.5%.
strings.h_ecMode: Net to gross: worked out exactly with 2026 tax brackets, credit points, NI, health and pension.
strings.h_ecOver: Equipment, office and admin, as % of gross
strings.h_ecPts: Resident 2.25, a woman 2.75, more for children, degree etc.
strings.h_enTerms: Each field also shows its English term – handy for newcomers and for dealing with people abroad.
strings.h_endMonth: Deposited at the end of each month
strings.h_evDiff: How much more the electric car costs to buy
strings.h_favCur: Ctrl or ⌘ to pick several. They appear first in lists and the table
strings.h_fee: Banks and card issuers typically charge 0.5% to 3%
strings.h_fiOther: Per month. Lowers the expenses the capital has to cover
strings.h_fiWd: 4% a year is common. Lower is more conservative and needs more capital.
strings.h_figMode: Automatic shows the official figures, read-only. Manual lets you change any of them, such as the credit point value, and the result uses only yours.
strings.h_flBill: How much of the time you can bill clients
strings.h_flBuf: Added to the rate for slow months and unpaid invoices
strings.h_frRaise: For example, raises. Leave 0 to be cautious.
strings.h_gdAlt: What the payments would earn if you saved them instead (deposit / money-market).
strings.h_gdDep: A new car loses about 15–20% a year at first.
strings.h_gdInc: How much more you will earn thanks to the study; checked over at least 10 years.
strings.h_gdRate: Use the true yearly cost, fees included.
strings.h_gdRet: Value growth + income (rent, profit) a year, after costs.
strings.h_gdUse: The question is not loan or no loan, but whether what it buys earns more than it costs.
strings.h_gkey: Your own key from aistudio.google.com. Stored only in this browser (encrypted when signed in) and left out of exports. Gemini can be wrong, so outlandish values are rejected.
strings.h_gkeyFree: For the assistant and explanations to work on this site, paste a free key from Google AI Studio. It stays in this browser, is left out of exports, and is sent only to Google.
strings.h_hfx: In holiday themes: flags, fireworks, snow, sparks and more. With reduced motion a still picture is shown.
strings.h_holAuto: During a holiday the app switches to its theme, then returns to your own. Dates follow the Hebrew, Hijri and Gregorian calendars.
strings.h_hzAlt: For example a broad index fund.
strings.h_hzCost: If the cost is higher than the value, the holding is at a loss.
strings.h_hzExp: Your yearly assumption. Nobody knows the future.
strings.h_hzGains: A loss on the sale can offset them and save tax this year.
strings.h_ifRet: The same return for every option, to see only the effect of fees.
strings.h_import: On the original device: Settings, Account, Move to another device. Paste the code here and enter the same username and password.
strings.h_inGroup: Typing 15000 shows 15,000. Calculations always use the number itself, so results do not change.
strings.h_inRate: Bank of Israel target: 1%–3%. 12 months to Aug 2026: 1.5%.
strings.h_insC: The sum insured or cover limit in the offer.
strings.h_insClaims: For the deductibles: e.g. 0.2 = one claim in five years. 0 = none.
strings.h_insCo: Add as many offers as you like. Pick an insurer or type your own name (✏️). Prices are what you typed from the offer – not the insurer's price list.
strings.h_insD: What you pay yourself on each claim.
strings.h_insE: Paid add-ons, such as a replacement car or transplants.
strings.h_insG: A "variable" premium rises with age, usually 3%–8% a year. Fixed premium: 0.
strings.h_insIdx: Most premiums are index-linked. Enter the expected inflation.
strings.h_insKind: The notes at the end match the type you choose.
strings.h_insP: The monthly premium in the offer.
strings.h_insX: A discount in the first years, after which the premium rises.
strings.h_insYears: For life, health and care use 10–20 years. For car and home one year is enough.
strings.h_kbLang: Off by default. When on: typing Hebrew, Arabic or English letters in a text field switches the app to that language. A browser cannot see which keyboard is open, so it goes by the letters you type.
strings.h_kqFx: If the platform works in dollars.
strings.h_kqSpread: The gap between the buy and sell price in the app. Often not shown as a fee.
strings.h_kqWd: A fixed amount in shekels, if you move coins to your own wallet.
strings.h_ksRet: Bank deposit: low fixed return; provident fund: depends on the track
strings.h_lBalloon: Spitzer only. For example 30: the monthly payment is lower, and 30% of the principal is paid in one go at the end. 100% is a full balloon (the "balloon" method).
strings.h_lBoi: Updates automatically from the Bank of Israel. Change it to try a scenario.
strings.h_lBoiChg: Prime moves with the Bank of Israel rate. 0 = stays as today. E.g. −0.25 if you expect a quarter-percent drop a year.
strings.h_lCpi: Updates automatically from the CPI over the last 12 months. Change it to test a scenario.
strings.h_lGraceType: In a full grace the interest is added to the debt, so the payments after it are higher.
strings.h_lLink: In a linked loan the balance rises with the CPI. The rate is usually lower, but the payment and the debt grow with inflation.
strings.h_lMargin: What the bank offered: e.g. prime minus 0.5 → -0.5, prime plus 1 → 1.
strings.h_lMode: Start from the amount or the payment that suits you – or check what interest an existing loan carries.
strings.h_lMonths: One payment a month: 12 payments = a year, 60 payments = 5 years. Change it here and the years update, and the other way round.
strings.h_lPAdd: What the bank adds on top of prime: plus 1 → 1, plus 2 → 2, minus 0.5 → -0.5.
strings.h_lPay: How much you want or can repay each month.
strings.h_lRateBank: The rate the bank gives you, as written in the offer or contract.
strings.h_lRateIn: Total – type the annual rate as it is. By parts – the Bank of Israel rate (updates by itself), the prime spread (1.5%), and what the bank adds, e.g. plus 1 or plus 2. The total is worked out for you.
strings.h_lRateType: Fixed – the same rate the whole time. Variable – reset every few years. Prime – the Bank of Israel rate + 1.5%, plus or minus the margin the bank gives you.
strings.h_lSpread: Prime in Israel = the Bank of Israel rate + 1.5%. Almost always 1.5.
strings.h_lVarChg: E.g. 0.5 if you expect the rate to rise half a percent at each reset, or negative if it falls. 0 = stays as today.
strings.h_lVarEvery: Usually every 5 years. At each reset the rate is set again by the market.
strings.h_langFallback: The interface is translated into every language. The first time you pick a new language the translation loads automatically and is saved on the device; numbers, currency names and text direction follow the language.
strings.h_live: Crypto prices update near real time. Regular currency rates update at the source only once a day, so they have no second-by-second refresh.
strings.h_liveFx: Works when the page can reach the rate server: a saved file or your own site. Inside claude.ai the connection is blocked.
strings.h_liveNoAcc: All sources are public and need no account. Inside claude.ai the page cannot reach outside sites, so official data reaches it through the app update once each business day, only for people signed in to claude.ai.
strings.h_lkFut: What the amount becomes if the index keeps rising as in the last 12 months.
strings.h_lkMonth: Contracts usually use the "known index": last month's index, published on the 15th.
strings.h_lmFund: On perpetuals you pay (or get) funding three times a day.
strings.h_lmLev: ×3 = a position three times your money.
strings.h_lmMm: When your equity falls below this share of the position, it is closed. Usually 25% for shares, often under 1% for crypto.
strings.h_lmRate: Charged on the borrowed part only.
strings.h_loc: Rate and ceiling depend on the locality. Enter them from the Tax Authority list
strings.h_ltBexp: Purchase tax, lawyer, agent and appraiser.
strings.h_ltCeil: This amount is updated over time. Check with the Tax Authority.
strings.h_ltCpi: Cumulative percentage, by the consumer price index.
strings.h_lvDiv: Commonly 25 for a 5-day week and 26 for a 6-day week. Check your contract.
strings.h_lvEnt: By law, seniority and work week, or your contract.
strings.h_lvYrs: 1 in the first year, 2 in the second, and so on.
strings.h_mc: Up to 3 tracks per offer – share, rate and term. A 0% track is skipped. Variable tracks assume the rate stays the same.
strings.h_mcCpi: Yearly inflation forecast – affects CPI-linked tracks
strings.h_mcPti: Bank of Israel caps it at 50%; banks prefer 30%-40%
strings.h_mktLive: In manual mode the app does not fetch rates and indices by itself; the last values stay and the refresh button updates once. Official daily figures still arrive.
strings.h_mmDep: The rate the bank offers on an unlinked shekel deposit.
strings.h_mmFee: Check your fund's fee; the value here is only an example.
strings.h_mmInfl: In the fund, tax is paid only on the real gain above inflation.
strings.h_mmYld: A money-market fund roughly tracks the Bank of Israel rate.
strings.h_mvAlert: When an index or commodity moves more than your threshold today – an alert with a sound (once a day each). Works while live data is on and the app or site is open.
strings.h_myEq: For example, to check how much mortgage you can get.
strings.h_myGross: Fills in salary, net and income in every calculator you have not changed yet.
strings.h_myKids: For the child allowance and family calculators.
strings.h_nwWd: How much of the investments you can take each year; 3%–4% is common
strings.h_oaBYear: From age 80 the pension is higher.
strings.h_oaSp: Qualifies for a spouse supplement, subject to an income test.
strings.h_oaYrs: Each year adds 2% seniority, up to 50%.
strings.h_opMult: For US share options, 100. In Tel Aviv it depends on the asset.
strings.h_opPrem: The option's price for one unit of the underlying.
strings.h_opS: The share or index the option is on.
strings.h_openSignup: When blocked, nobody can create a new account in this browser. Someone with access to the browser can still bypass this, so also restrict the link in the Share menu.
strings.h_ot125: The first two extra hours each day
strings.h_otSh: Work on the weekly rest day
strings.h_otherCredits: For example pension, donations or a qualifying locality
strings.h_pc: Type the fees from your offer. Names are for convenience only. Check "Gemel Net" by the Ministry of Finance.
strings.h_pcRet: Expected yearly return before fees. Can be set per offer.
strings.h_pfOther: Affects the tax bracket of the pension.
strings.h_pfSev: Each such shekel takes ₪1.35 off the exemption.
strings.h_pfShare: The rest stays for tax-free lump-sum withdrawals.
strings.h_plain: Under professional terms (gross, prime, index linkage and more) a short explanation in simple words appears.
strings.h_ppFee: Comes out of the available cash, so less goes to the loan
strings.h_prBoi: Updates automatically from the Bank of Israel. Change it to test a scenario.
strings.h_prDRate: E.g. −0.5 for an expected half-point cut.
strings.h_prMargin: E.g. −0.5 for prime minus half, or 6 for prime plus 6. Your margin is in the loan agreement or account statement.
strings.h_prTax: Non-linked shekel deposit: 15% of the interest.
strings.h_profile: Filled in automatically in salary, income tax, self-employed and rental
strings.h_ptMode: Used by every calculator with credit points: salary, income tax, self-employed, rent, severance, tax refund and more.
strings.h_ptOther: One-off amount added to the total cost
strings.h_ptVal: Pick "My own value" and type it in. The change is kept only for you.
strings.h_pzRisk: 0.5%–2% of the portfolio per trade is common.
strings.h_pzStop: Below the entry for a long, above it for a short.
strings.h_rateSrc: The source is used only where the page may call external servers
strings.h_rblAdd: You can rebalance with new money only, without selling.
strings.h_rentDep: Usually 2% of the building value, excluding land
strings.h_res: 30+ days last year earn credit points: 30–39 days = 0.5, 40–49 = 0.75, 50 = 1, plus 0.25 per 5 more days, up to 4 points (110 days). You need IDF confirmation and Form 101 for your employer.
strings.h_rfPen: Including any rate-difference charge by the bank.
strings.h_rsInc: Employee: gross from payslips. Self-employed: from advance payments. No income – you get the minimum.
strings.h_rsKids: Qualifies for the daily family grant.
strings.h_rsUnit: The daily grants depend on the unit rank. If unsure – usually B/C.
strings.h_rtCoef: The number the balance is divided by to get a monthly pension, usually 190–220 in pension funds. 0 = hide
strings.h_rtNeed: In today’s money. It is adjusted for inflation.
strings.h_rtOther: State pension or similar, in today’s money. Leave 0 if unknown.
strings.h_sAbsD: Deducted from the salary at a day's value.
strings.h_sAdv: Taken off the net on this payslip.
strings.h_sAge: 2026 National Insurance and health rates change with age. Under 18 and old-age pensioners pay nothing from pay.
strings.h_sCar: The car benefit is added to your pay for tax, so net pay drops even if you pay nothing for the car
strings.h_sCarBr: Automatic taxes the benefit at the brackets your pay reaches. Manual taxes all of it at the rate you pick.
strings.h_sCarExtra: For example fuel over the quota, Highway 6, fines or private trips taken from your pay
strings.h_sCarGil: With a gross-up the employer adds an amount to the payslip that covers the tax on the car
strings.h_sCarMode: In automatic mode the price and engine type come from the official price list, and the value follows the 2026 rules.
strings.h_sCarPay: What is taken from your pay for the car. It lowers the benefit value
strings.h_sCarVal: The amount on the payslip as "car benefit", after any green-car reduction.
strings.h_sComm: Sales or target commissions this month.
strings.h_sCoord: The rate on the Tax Authority coordination approval.
strings.h_sDkids: 2 credit points for each child recognised as having a disability.
strings.h_sDon: A donation to an approved body gives a 35% tax credit, above the yearly minimum and up to 30% of income.
strings.h_sErDis: The employer's payment for disability insurance. Usually up to 2.5% of salary is tax-free.
strings.h_sExtra: Taxed and subject to National Insurance, but no pension is deducted from them.
strings.h_sGift: A gift from the employer counts as income for tax (a benefit), even with no cash.
strings.h_sGlobalOt: A fixed amount for overtime, regardless of actual hours.
strings.h_sHavDay: ₪451.50 a day in the private sector (2026). The public sector differs.
strings.h_sHavraa: The yearly amount on the payslip; spread over 12 months here.
strings.h_sHolD: For hourly workers after 3 months: up to 9 holiday days a year.
strings.h_sHours: A full-time job is 182 hours a month.
strings.h_sJob: A second job without tax coordination: the top rate and no credit points. With coordination, type the approved rate.
strings.h_sLoanDed: A monthly payment taken off the net.
strings.h_sLoc: Residents of a qualifying town get a tax discount up to a yearly cap. The rate and cap are in the Tax Authority list of towns.
strings.h_sMeals: A cash addition that is taxed.
strings.h_sMournD: Up to 7 paid mourning days for a close relative (hourly workers).
strings.h_sOleh: Credit points by the month since aliyah (Kol Zchut).
strings.h_sOlehM: From 2022: 1/12 point a month in year one, 1/4 to month 30, 1/6 to month 42 and 1/12 to month 54.
strings.h_sOncall: Pay for being available outside working hours.
strings.h_sOt: The first two extra hours a day are at 125%, from the third at 150%.
strings.h_sOtherDed: Amounts taken off the payslip after tax. They do not change the tax.
strings.h_sPayType: Hourly pay counts actual hours; vacation, holidays and sick days are paid separately.
strings.h_sPhone: The phone benefit is added to income for tax.
strings.h_sReimb: Work expenses repaid against receipts, like travel or parking. Added to the net, not taxed.
strings.h_sReserveD: During reserve duty the employer keeps paying in full and National Insurance repays it. On hourly pay – at a day's value.
strings.h_sRoleAdd: A fixed addition for a role, responsibility or profession.
strings.h_sSenior: Sets how many vacation and recuperation days you get.
strings.h_sSeniorPay: A fixed addition for years of service, if your agreement has one.
strings.h_sShab: Work on the rest day is paid at least 150%.
strings.h_sShift: Extra pay for evening or night shifts.
strings.h_sSickBal: You build up 1.5 days a month, up to 90.
strings.h_sSickD: By the Sick Pay Law: day 1 unpaid, days 2–3 at 50%, from day 4 at 100%.
strings.h_sSickPay: Some employers and agreements pay in full from day 1.
strings.h_sTravel: Taxed and subject to National Insurance, with no pension deduction.
strings.h_sUnion: A share of pay, e.g. 0.8%. Taken from net pay.
strings.h_sVacBal: As shown on last month's payslip.
strings.h_sVacD: On a monthly salary vacation is already in the pay; on hourly pay it is paid separately. It comes off your vacation balance.
strings.h_sVacRed: Vacation days paid out in cash (usually when leaving). Taxable.
strings.h_sWdays: Used to work out a day's value on a monthly salary (usually 21–23).
strings.h_sWfh: Help with internet, electricity and so on. Taxable.
strings.h_sep: Applies to every number in the app: results and the fields you type in.
strings.h_sexDef: Sets the base points in salary, income tax, self-employed and rental
strings.h_sgTax: Capital gains tax paid on the gain at the end (usually 25%)
strings.h_shareLang: The app stays in your language; whatever you copy, share or save as PDF comes out in the language picked here.
strings.h_signupAll: When blocked, nobody can sign up or add a new account on any device, not via new phone, cloud sign-in or recovery either. The block is stored in the cloud and only you, the app owner, can change it. Existing users keep signing in as usual.
strings.h_signupByOwner: The app owner has blocked new sign-ups, and only the owner can reopen them.
strings.h_signupDev: When blocked, no new account can be created or added on this device, not via new phone or recovery either. Only {n} can change this setting.

strings.kb_avgcost: When you buy an asset in several rounds at different prices, the average cost is total invested divided by units. Investing a fixed amount monthly spreads timing risk.
strings.kb_betterment: Tax on the gain from selling a home or land. Sellers of a sole residence can be exempt under certain conditions.
strings.kb_boi: The rate the Bank of Israel sets about eight times a year to cool or boost the economy. It drives prime, mortgages and the interest you earn on deposits.
strings.kb_brackets: Israeli income tax is progressive: each slice of income is taxed at its own bracket rate. Moving into a higher bracket only raises tax on the part above it, not on your whole salary.
strings.kb_breakeven: The volume or revenue at which a business exactly covers all its costs. Above it, you start making a profit.
strings.kb_btl: Payroll deductions that fund benefits (unemployment, maternity, disability, old age and more) and the health system. The rate is low on the first part of your pay and higher above it.
strings.kb_capgain: Tax on the real gain from selling shares, funds, crypto and other assets — usually 25%. Losses can be offset against gains in the same year.
strings.kb_compound: When earnings are added to the principal and start earning too. The longer the time, the bigger the effect — so starting early matters far more than the deposit size.
strings.kb_cpi: A monthly index from the Central Bureau of Statistics that tracks prices of a basket of goods and services. "CPI-linked" loans and savings are updated by it.
strings.kb_credit: A credit or instalment deal with interest adds cost to a purchase. Check the effective rate and the total you will pay before agreeing.
strings.kb_crypto: Digital currencies like Bitcoin whose prices swing widely. In Israel, gains from selling or swapping them are subject to capital gains tax.
strings.kb_debt: Two common methods: the "snowball" pays the smallest debt first for momentum; the "avalanche" pays the highest-interest debt first, saving more interest.
strings.kb_div: Part of a company's profit paid out to shareholders. In Israel it is usually taxed at 25%, and 30% for a major shareholder.
strings.kb_effective: The true yearly cost of a loan, including fees and payment frequency. It is the right way to compare offers from different banks.
strings.kb_emergency: Cash set aside for emergencies, usually 3–6 months of expenses, so a lost income or a sudden bill does not push you into debt.
strings.kb_equal: Each month you repay the same share of principal plus interest. Payments start high and fall over time, and total interest is lower than with Spitzer.
strings.kb_fire: Saving and investing hard to reach financial independence and retire early. A common rule of thumb: build 25 times your yearly spending (the "4% rule").
strings.kb_gross: Gross is pay before deductions. Net is what reaches your account after income tax, National Insurance, health tax and the pension contribution.
strings.kb_hishtalmut: A medium-term savings fund your employer pays into, usually available after 6 years. Up to a ceiling its gains are free of capital gains tax — one of the most worthwhile savings.
strings.kb_infl: A general rise in prices over time. With 3% inflation, ₪100 buys next year roughly what ₪97 buys today — so money that is not invested loses value.
strings.kb_lease: Renting a car for a fixed term with a monthly payment. Compare the full cost, including any down payment and end-of-term payment, with buying in cash or on finance.
strings.kb_leave: Paid days off that build up with seniority and job scope. Unused days are paid out when the job ends.
strings.kb_linked: In a CPI-linked loan the balance is updated by the price index. With inflation, the debt and the payment grow even if the rate is fixed.
strings.kb_mortgage: A home loan secured by the home itself. In Israel it is usually built from several tracks, each with its own rate and linkage.
strings.kb_networth: Everything you own (savings, investments, home) minus everything you owe (mortgage, loans). The best measure of your finances and progress over time.
strings.kb_notice: How far in advance whoever ends the employment (employee or employer) must give notice. It depends on seniority and on monthly versus hourly pay.
strings.kb_pension: Mandatory retirement savings: you and your employer put a share of your salary in every month (including a severance part), and it is invested until retirement. Low management fees make a big difference to the final amount.
strings.kb_points: Points that lower your monthly income tax. Each point has a fixed value updated every year, given for residency, gender, children, a degree, army and reserve service and more. Enter yours in the personal profile in Settings.
strings.kb_prepay: A fee the bank may charge when you repay a loan early, mainly on fixed-rate tracks when market rates have fallen since you took it.
strings.kb_prime: The base rate Israeli banks charge on loans. It is always the Bank of Israel rate plus 1.5%, so when the Bank of Israel changes its rate, prime and every loan tied to it change right away.
strings.kb_purchase: Tax paid when buying a home or property. A sole home has lenient brackets; investors and additional homes pay more.
strings.kb_rate: The official exchange rate the Bank of Israel publishes every business day. Banks, exchange offices and card companies add a margin, so the rate you get differs a little.
strings.kb_refi: Replacing your current mortgage with a new one on better terms. Compare the interest saved with the early-repayment fee and costs.
strings.kb_rental: Residential rent has three options: exemption up to a monthly ceiling, a 10% track on gross income, or regular bracket tax with expenses deducted. The calculator compares them.
strings.kb_rentbuy: Comparing renting and investing your equity with buying on a mortgage. The answer depends on interest rates, the alternative return on your money and house-price growth.
strings.kb_reserve: Active reservists can get extra credit points based on the days they served the previous year. Enter the days in the personal profile in Settings and the calculation includes them.
strings.kb_savegoal: An amount you want to reach by a certain date. The calculator shows how much to put aside each month, allowing for returns and inflation.
strings.kb_selfemp: An exempt dealer charges no VAT and has a yearly turnover cap; a licensed dealer charges VAT and offsets VAT on expenses. Both pay their own income tax and National Insurance.
strings.kb_severance: Usually one month's salary per year worked, for an employee who was dismissed and in some cases one who resigned. Part of it is tax-free up to a ceiling.
strings.kb_spitzer: A repayment method with a fixed monthly payment. At first most of it is interest; later most of it reduces the principal.
strings.kb_switched: Language switched to match your keyboard
strings.kb_tracks: The main tracks: prime (floats with prime), fixed unlinked, fixed CPI-linked, and variable every five years. A good mix balances a stable payment against total cost.
strings.kb_vat: A tax added to most goods and services. In Israel it is 18% (since January 2025): price with VAT = price × 1.18, price before VAT = price ÷ 1.18.
strings.kb_yield: The gain from an investment as a percentage over a period. An average yearly return lets you compare investments held for different lengths of time.

strings.lg_a_contact: Found an accessibility problem or have a suggestion? Write to us through "Feedback to the developer" in Settings → System, saying which screen and what the problem is. We will look into it and try to fix it soon.
strings.lg_a_d1: Screen readers: headings, labels for fields and buttons, and announcements for results that update.
strings.lg_a_d10: A floating accessibility button on every screen: text up to 175%, high contrast, readable font, stopping animations, highlighted links and focus, text spacing, grayscale, a big cursor and reading the screen aloud.
strings.lg_a_d11: Direct printing from every screen: a clean report with real tables (not an image) that screen readers can follow, a large print text option, a high-contrast black-and-white mode, and an options window that works fully by keyboard. The printer is chosen in the device's own print window, which is accessible in itself.
strings.lg_a_d12: Signing scanned documents three ways – drawing, typing a name, or photographing a signature on paper – so people who find drawing on a screen hard can still sign. The signature's position and size can also be set by keyboard (arrows, + and −).
strings.lg_a_d13: The PDF editor works by keyboard too: every tool has a spoken name, the "items on the page" list lets you pick any item without touching the screen, and moving, resizing, deleting, undo and redo all work with keys. Text and a typed signature can be added instead of drawing.
strings.lg_a_d14: Files open through "Share" from other apps too, batch scanning works with a normal button as well as automatic capture, and a PDF from a scan can carry a text layer that screen readers can read. A "Scan" button sits in the header of every calculator.
strings.lg_a_d15: QR codes, file conversion and the document scanner never require a camera: you can choose a picture or file from the device, scan results appear as text that can be read aloud and copied, and every button is labelled and keyboard-operable.
strings.lg_a_d2: Keyboard-only use, with a clear mark of where you are on the screen.
strings.lg_a_d3: High contrast, light or dark colours and a readable font – in Settings → Display & language.
strings.lg_a_d4: Changing text size, and browser zoom up to 200% without losing content.
strings.lg_a_d7: Three languages – Hebrew, Arabic and English – each in its correct direction.
strings.lg_a_d8: Works on phones and small screens, with buttons sized for touch.
strings.lg_a_d9: In the document scanner the document type is chosen from labelled choice buttons, and the corner dots can also be moved with the keyboard (arrow keys).
strings.lg_a_how: The accessibility button (♿) is on every screen and opens every adjustment in one place. They are also under Settings → Display & language, Settings → Sounds and Settings → System. Adjustments are saved on the device and apply everywhere. The app can also be installed on the home screen and opened like any app.
strings.lg_a_intro: The financial calculator is meant for everyone, including people with disabilities. It is built as far as possible to Israeli Standard 5568 (based on WCAG 2.0 level AA), we aim to meet WCAG 2.1 as well, and we keep improving it with every version.
strings.lg_a_l1: In charts some information is visual. The main values also appear as text or in a table.
strings.lg_a_l2: Content from outside sites is not under our control and may not be fully accessible.
strings.lg_a_l3: PDFs made from pictures (scans, the CV, compressed PDFs or "flat" saving) are images that screen readers can't read. Scans can get a text layer ("Searchable PDF"), and print reports are printed as real text.
strings.lg_a_l4: Freehand drawing needs touch or a mouse; every drawing has an alternative (text, a mark, a shape). A scanned PDF with no text layer can't be read by screen readers – its text can be extracted in the scanner.
strings.lg_a_l5: The accessibility of external tools – the device keyboard, print window, camera, share sheet and file-save window – depends on your operating system and browser.

strings.lg_p_contact: Privacy questions or a request about your information – through "Feedback to the developer" in Settings → System.
strings.lg_p_dev1: Your settings and the data you enter – in the calculators, CV, accounting and lists – are kept only in your device's browser, in its local storage. The app uses no cookies.
strings.lg_p_dev10: Bank accounts adviser: nicknames, balances and amounts are kept on the device only. The tool has no field for an account or branch number. Only nicknames and amounts go to the assistant, and only when you tap "Ask the assistant".
strings.lg_p_dev11: Fuel calculator: the fill-up log (date, odometer, litres and amount) and your car details are kept on the device only. You can export the log to a file or delete it.
strings.lg_p_dev12: Reminders: titles, dates and notes are kept on the device only. A calendar file (.ics) is made only when you ask.
strings.lg_p_dev13: Documents & receipts: receipt details are kept on the device and photos in the browser's own storage (IndexedDB) – not in private mode or an encrypted account. A document check sends photos to the AI only when you tap.
strings.lg_p_dev14: Insights, rights, planning, family, trips and savings: everything you enter is kept on the device only. In the couple budget, expenses travel only as an encrypted message you make and pass on yourself.
strings.lg_p_dev15: Sharing the whole picture with the assistant is off by default. When it's on, a summary of spending, reminders and savings is sent with the question to the AI engine you chose.
strings.lg_p_dev2: When you sign in, your data is encrypted on the device (AES-GCM, with a key derived from your password). The account itself is local: we have no account server and cannot see your data or recover a password.
strings.lg_p_dev3: A Gemini key, if you saved one, stays only on the device and is left out of exports.
strings.lg_p_dev4: The document scanner: a personal card (ID, passport, licence and more) is processed only on the phone – cropping, straightening, hiding details and the watermark – with no AI and nothing sent anywhere, and the scan is not kept in the app. Only the file you chose to download or share remains. In the payslip check only the numbers are kept on the device, and you can delete them on that screen.
strings.lg_p_dev5: Tax Free: the purchases you enter are kept on the device. Personal details for the form (name, address and so on) are kept only if you tick "remember". The app has no field for a passport, ID, card or bank account number. When the form is prepared with AI, the details you filled in are sent only to translate them.
strings.lg_p_dev6: Printing: the print page is built inside the browser and deleted as soon as printing ends. The app doesn't send it to any server or keep it. You choose the printer in the device's print window, and the app can't see which printer you picked. If you choose a network printer or a cloud print service, the printout goes through it under its own terms.
strings.lg_p_dev7: Signature: the signature you draw, type or photograph is made and placed on the device and is never sent to any server or AI. It is kept on the device only if you tick "remember", separately from the settings and backups – so it isn't included in a backup file or a settings export. "Delete the saved signature" removes it at once.
strings.lg_p_dev8: The PDF editor, conversions and QR codes: files are opened, edited and converted on your phone only and never sent to a server. The camera runs only while scanning, its pictures aren't kept, and links from codes open only when you tap. To show and write PDFs, open-source libraries (pdf.js, pdf-lib, JSZip) load from our site; in the Claude app they load from jsDelivr, which – like any website – sees the request's IP address, but not your files. Only "read the text" sends scanned pages to the AI, and only when you tap it.
strings.lg_p_dev9: The editor's draft is kept on the device (IndexedDB) so you can continue later, and is deleted when the file is saved or closed or you tap "Delete the draft". In private mode and with an encrypted account no draft is kept. Files shared to the app are held for a moment in the browser's cache and deleted as soon as they open.
strings.lg_p_devH: What is kept on your device
strings.lg_p_ext0: Requests for prices and rates go straight from your device, with no cookies and no details about you. A site receiving a request sees your IP address, as with any browsing. Fonts load through the app's own server.
strings.lg_p_ext1: Rates and prices: Bank of Israel, the CBS, the European Central Bank (via Frankfurter), ExchangeRate-API, gold-api, Coinbase, Binance and similar sources.
strings.lg_p_ext2: Fonts: loaded from the site itself; the browser does not contact an outside service for them.
strings.lg_p_ext3: AI, only when you use it: the text you wrote and, when scanning, the photo (a payslip, an offer, an exercise, a letter to translate, or any document with auto-detect) is sent to Claude in the Claude app, or to Google's Gemini with your own key (in developer and family mode). The app does not keep the photo, the letter or the translation; for a payslip only the numbers are kept, on the device. Cover identifying details before taking the photo.
strings.lg_p_ext4: A question to the assistant in an outside service (ChatGPT, Perplexity and the like) opens there only when you choose it.
strings.lg_p_ext5: Requests to outside services are sent without cookies and without telling them which site they come from.
strings.lg_p_ext6: The website is hosted by a cloud hosting provider, which sees your IP address each time the site loads, under its privacy policy. The code and shared data (rates, indices) are kept in a code repository and reach the site from there. The previous address forwards here and, with one tap, moves your data too – directly on your phone.
strings.lg_p_ext7: Cloud sync (only if you turned it on): a copy of the account data is kept on our server, locked with your password on the phone itself. Neither the server nor the site's owner can read it. The account is identified by a one-way fingerprint of the username; no name, email or IP address is kept. Sync can be stopped, or the copy deleted, at any time in Settings › Account. The same applies to documents you upload.
strings.lg_p_ext8: Share prices: when you ask to update prices, our server sends a free public source only the symbol, nothing about you.
strings.lg_p_intro: The calculator is built so your information stays with you. There are no ads, no tracking or usage statistics, and we do not sell or pass on information to anyone.
strings.lg_p_law: This policy follows Israel's Protection of Privacy Law, 1981, and its regulations. There is no legal obligation to give us any information: anything sent (feedback, an AI question, a nickname) is sent by your choice, used only for the purpose you sent it for, and not passed to others beyond the services listed here. Every calculator can be used without providing any information.
strings.lg_p_no: No ads, no tracking or analytics tools, no selling information and no profiling.
strings.lg_p_perm: Camera – only when you tap a camera scan (documents, batch scanning, QR); pictures are neither kept nor sent. Location – only when you tap "My location" while making a QR code, and it goes only into the code. Notifications and sharing – only when you ask. You can revoke permissions at any time in your browser or phone settings.
strings.lg_p_priv: In Settings → Security you can turn on a mode in which the app contacts no outside site. Prices then come from the site's own automatic update.
strings.lg_p_r1: Delete everything on the device: Settings → System → Data and reset, or delete the account in Settings → Account & access.
strings.lg_p_r2: Get a copy of your data: "Backup and restore" in Settings → System.
strings.lg_p_r3: Ask to see, correct or delete feedback you sent: write to us through the feedback form.
strings.lg_p_sec: The site loads only over an encrypted connection (HTTPS) with security headers. We have no user database. Accounts are encrypted on the device, and feedback on the site is encrypted before it leaves the device. Nobody – not even the developer – can see the data on your device.
strings.lg_p_us1: Feedback: only what you write in the form and, if you choose, a signed name and/or an e-mail address for a reply. On the website the message is encrypted on your device and sent through a relay service (ntfy.sh), and only the developer can open it. In the Claude app it is kept in the app's database, visible only to the developer.
strings.lg_p_us2: A handle, if you chose one: kept only as a hash, so no one else can take it.
strings.lg_p_us3: Family mode: only a hash of the sign-in is kept, with no names and no list of who is connected.
strings.lg_p_us4: Nothing else is collected: no location, no device model and no usage history.
strings.lg_p_us5: Automatic crash reports: if something crashes on the site, an anonymous technical report is sent to us so we can fix it – the error text, the screen, the version, the language and the system and browser type (for example Android · Chrome). No name, email, IP address, data you typed or calculations. In full private mode nothing is sent.
strings.lg_t_ai: AI answers, explanations, scanning, letter translations, draft replies and exercise solutions can be wrong, even when checked by the calculator. An AI translation is not a certified or official translation, and an explanation of a letter is not legal advice. Check any important result against the original.
strings.lg_t_beta: The app is in development (beta) and is updated all the time. Features, calculations, data and screens may change, break or stop without notice, and it may contain faults and mistakes. Check any important result against another source.
strings.lg_t_calc1: Results are an estimate based on the data you entered and the rules built into the app, and may differ from reality.
strings.lg_t_calc2: All information, calculations and results in the app are general information only. They are not investment advice, investment marketing, pension, tax, insurance or legal advice, and are not tailored to any person's data, needs or situation. Do not rely on them when making decisions. Before any financial decision, consult a suitably licensed professional (investment adviser, pension adviser, tax adviser, insurance agent or lawyer).
strings.lg_t_chg: The app, its features and these terms may change or stop at any time. The current version is always shown here, and every change to the terms is recorded in the update history at the end.
strings.lg_t_contact: Questions about these terms – through the feedback form in Settings → System.
strings.lg_t_data: Prices come from outside sources and may be delayed, incomplete or wrong. Do not rely on them for trading or transactions.
strings.lg_t_host: The site is hosted by outside providers. The address may change; when it does, the previous address forwards to the new one and lets you move the data on your device. Continuous availability isn't guaranteed, and provider outages may take the site down temporarily.
strings.lg_t_intro: The financial calculator is a free tool for calculations, documents and general information that runs in the browser and in the Claude app. Using it means you accept these terms. If you don't agree, please don't use the app.
strings.lg_t_ip: The app's code, design and content belong to the developer. Open-source libraries and fonts are used under their licences, listed under "Licences and credits". Documents, pictures and data you create or upload remain yours.
strings.lg_t_law: These terms are governed by the laws of the State of Israel. If any clause is found invalid, the rest continue to apply.
strings.lg_t_liab: The app is provided as is, with no promise that it will always work, be free of faults or be accurate. You use it at your own risk, and there is no liability for direct or indirect damage from using or relying on it.
strings.lg_t_lic: The app's operators are not licensed under the Israeli Regulation of Investment Advice, Investment Marketing and Portfolio Management Law, 1995, nor under the Supervision of Financial Services (Pension Advice, Marketing and Clearing System) Law, 2005. The app therefore gives no investment advice or investment marketing, and no pension advice or pension marketing.
strings.lg_t_pdf: Editing and converting documents: you are responsible for a document's content and the changes you make. Don't alter an official document, contract or signed document to mislead, present an edited copy as the original, or forge. Conversion between formats is best-effort – complex layouts may change, so check the result before sending. "White-out" only hides; for real removal use redaction or "flat" saving.
strings.lg_t_prn: A printout from the app is a copy of the calculation or document at the moment it was printed. It isn't an official confirmation, an invoice or an original document, and its figures are estimates only. Printed scans of cards and documents must not be presented as originals or used to forge them.
strings.lg_t_qr: QR codes: the link check before opening catches common signs of fake sites, but it can't guarantee a site is safe. Don't enter passwords or payment details on a site you reached from a code you aren't sure about. Codes you create are your responsibility – check they scan properly before printing.
strings.lg_t_sig: The signature in the document scanner is a simple electronic signature – an image of a signature placed on the document. It is not a "secure" or "certified" electronic signature under Israel's Electronic Signature Law, 2001, and no certificate or certifying authority stands behind it. Some bodies (courts, banks, authorities) may require a certified signature, a wet signature or extra identification, and it is your responsibility to check. Sign only in your own name or with explicit permission; the tool must not be used to forge someone else's signature or to change a document that has already been signed.
strings.lg_t_stamp: Stamps and page numbers are your own marks on the document. Don't use a stamp ("paid", "approved", "copy" and so on) to create a false impression, or stamp in another body's name.
strings.lg_t_tf: Tax Free calculations are estimates: eligibility, minimums, fees and the final amount are set by the shop, the refund company and the authorities in each country, so confirm them on the spot.
strings.lg_t_use1: Do not use the app for anything unlawful or to harm others.
strings.lg_t_use2: Do not try to get around its security, developer mode or family mode.
strings.lg_t_use3: What you enter and upload (for example for a CV) is your responsibility and stays on your device.
strings.lg_t_use4: Scanning personal cards and documents (ID, passport, licence and the like) is for your own documents or ones whose owners let you scan them. Do not use it to forge, alter or impersonate.

strings.lt_balloonC: Where the large sum at the end will come from, and how much interest you pay in all – usually more.
strings.lt_balloonD: Each month you pay only interest, and the whole principal (or part of it) at the end.
strings.lt_businessC: Personal guarantees, security, and whether the payment fits the business cash flow.
strings.lt_businessD: A loan for a business or the self-employed, sometimes state-guaranteed and with a grace period at first.
strings.lt_carC: What the car will be worth when the balloon is due, and the true rate against dealer finance.
strings.lt_carD: A loan to buy a car, sometimes with a balloon at the end and the car as security.
strings.lt_depositC: The gap between the rate you earn on the deposit and the rate you pay – sometimes it is better simply to break the deposit.
strings.lt_depositD: The deposit stays and earns, and the bank lends against it – usually at a low rate.
strings.lt_done: The calculator is set. The rate was not changed – enter the offer you got.
strings.lt_fixedC: Usually dearer than a variable rate, sometimes with a higher early-repayment fee.
strings.lt_fixedD: The rate does not change for the whole term – the payment is known up front.
strings.lt_graceC: How much the payment rises after the grace, and whether the interest is added to the debt.
strings.lt_graceD: For the first months you pay only interest (partial) or nothing (full), then repayment starts.
strings.lt_hishC: If the fund is already available, compare with withdrawing; and check whether the loan is balloon or Spitzer.
strings.lt_hishD: The fund keeps growing, and the manager lends against it, usually at a rate tied to prime or the index.
strings.lt_intro: A small repeated expense adds up to a big sum, especially when the money compounds.
strings.lt_mortgageC: The mix of tracks, the payment-to-income ratio, and the allowed financing share.
strings.lt_mortgageD: A loan for a home, in several tracks, with the home as security. It has its own calculator.
strings.lt_nonbankC: That the lender is licensed, the full effective rate, and opening and collection fees.
strings.lt_nonbankD: A loan from a credit company or a lender that is not a bank – usually faster and dearer.
strings.lt_note: You don't have to give it all up – even half the habit makes a difference.
strings.lt_personalC: The true rate with fees (effective rate), the early-repayment fee, and any required insurance.
strings.lt_personalD: A loan for any purpose, usually for a few years, with a fixed monthly payment.
strings.lt_pick: Pick a kind for an explanation
strings.lt_primeC: The margin over prime, and what happens to the payment if the rate rises by one or two points.
strings.lt_primeD: The rate is prime plus or minus a margin, and moves when the Bank of Israel changes its rate.
strings.lt_spitzerC: Compare with "equal principal": a higher payment at first, but less interest in all.
strings.lt_spitzerD: The common method: the same payment each month. At first it is mostly interest, at the end mostly principal.
strings.lt_variableC: How often the rate changes, by what, and whether you can leave without a fee at the reset.
strings.lt_variableD: The rate resets every few years by an anchor, so the payment can go up or down.

strings.lx_aprW: Also called the "effective rate". It includes opening fees and linkage, so it is the right number for comparing offers from different banks.
strings.lx_ask: What did the bank offer you? Pick one or type it above
strings.lx_boiW: The base rate of the whole economy. The Bank of Israel sets it several times a year to control inflation (rising prices). When it goes up, almost all bank loans get more expensive; when it goes down, they get cheaper.
strings.lx_boiYours: You chose to test a scenario. Today it is {r}.
strings.lx_chipsAria: What the bank offered: prime plus or minus
strings.lx_fine: General information and an estimate, not financial advice. The binding offer is the one in your contract with the bank.
strings.lx_g_aprD: The nominal rate is the number the bank writes. The effective rate also includes compounding, fees and linkage – that is the number to compare between offers.
strings.lx_g_bullet: Bullet / balloon – the principal at the end
strings.lx_g_bulletD: Each month you pay only interest, and the whole amount you borrowed is repaid at the end in one go. A low monthly payment, but you must be ready for a large payment at the end.
strings.lx_g_cpi: Linked to the consumer price index
strings.lx_g_cpiD: When prices in the economy rise (inflation), your remaining debt grows by the same percentage. The rate looks lower, but you can end up paying more. Always check the total cost with expected linkage.
strings.lx_g_equalD: Each month you repay the same part of the principal, so the payment is higher at first and falls over time. In total you pay less interest than with Spitzer.
strings.lx_g_extraD: Every extra shekel lowers the principal and so saves interest. Even a small amount saves a lot over the years.
strings.lx_g_feesD: A file-opening fee, an appraisal, insurance and fixed costs. They aren't part of the rate, but they are part of the loan's real price.
strings.lx_g_fixD: The same rate from the first day to the last. Plus: full certainty. Minus: usually more expensive, and early repayment can cost a fee.
strings.lx_g_graceD: A period at the start when you pay only interest. It gives breathing room, but the loan costs more and the later payments are higher.
strings.lx_g_h: 📚 Every loan option – what it is and what it means
strings.lx_g_insD: For large loans, especially mortgages, the bank requires life insurance and property insurance. You may compare and buy the insurance outside the bank.
strings.lx_g_intro: Every term in a bank's offer, in plain words.
strings.lx_g_nolinkD: The debt goes down only by what you pay. Simple and predictable.
strings.lx_g_preD: Repaying part or all of the loan ahead of time. Afterwards you can shorten the term or lower the monthly payment. Check whether there is an early-repayment fee, mainly with a fixed rate.
strings.lx_g_primeD: The rate moves every time the Bank of Israel changes its rate. Early repayment usually has no significant fee. The risk: if rates in the economy rise, so does the monthly payment.
strings.lx_g_q1D: Is it fixed, variable or prime, and what is the margin (for example prime + 2)?
strings.lx_g_q2: What is the real yearly cost?
strings.lx_g_q2D: Ask for the effective rate including all fees, and the total of all payments to the end.
strings.lx_g_q3: Is the loan linked to the index?
strings.lx_g_q3D: If so, ask for a calculation with expected inflation, not just 0%.
strings.lx_g_q4D: Ask about the early-repayment fee and when you can repay without it.
strings.lx_g_q5: Can I get a better offer?
strings.lx_g_q5D: Compare at least 2–3 banks or lenders. Show the bank a competing offer – the margin is exactly where you negotiate.
strings.lx_g_spitzerD: The same payment every month. At first most of it goes to interest and little to the principal (the amount you borrowed); at the end, the reverse. The most common.
strings.lx_g_varD: The rate is set again at fixed points, for example every 5 years, by the market at that time. At a reset point you can usually also repay without a high fee.
strings.lx_intro: This is how a loan's interest is built: from the Bank of Israel rate, through prime, to what the bank offers you.
strings.lx_offAbove: The margin (the bank's addition): {m}% above prime
strings.lx_offBelow: The margin (the bank's discount): {m}% below prime
strings.lx_offFlat: Exactly prime, with no addition and no discount
strings.lx_offerW: "Prime plus 2" means prime and another 2%. "Prime minus 0.5" means prime less half a percent. The addition or discount is called the margin, and it depends on the risk the bank sees in you, the collateral (for example a flat), the term – and negotiation. The margin stays the same for the whole loan, but prime itself can move.
strings.lx_offerWfix: A fixed rate stays the same for the whole term, even if the Bank of Israel changes its rate. A variable rate is set again every few years by the market. Comparing with prime helps you see whether the offer is expensive or cheap.
strings.lx_primeW: Prime is the base rate banks in Israel lend at. It is always 1.5% above the Bank of Israel rate and moves up and down with it. A "prime loan" means a rate that changes every time the Bank of Israel changes its rate.
strings.lx_say: The bank offered prime {m}, which means: {p} {m} = {r} a year
strings.lx_spreadSub: The same at every bank in Israel
strings.lx_spreadW: Banks in Israel calculate prime like this: the Bank of Israel rate plus 1.5%. This addition is fixed and doesn't change, so prime is always 1.5% above the Bank of Israel rate. It is not the margin the bank gives you – the margin comes in the next step.
strings.lx_yourFix: Doesn't change until the end of the loan
strings.lx_yourW: This is the loan's yearly rate today, and the monthly payment above is calculated from it. If the Bank of Israel raises or cuts its rate, your rate and your monthly payment change by the same amount.
strings.lx_yourWfix: This is the yearly rate the monthly payment is calculated from. With a fixed rate you know in advance exactly what you will pay, but it is usually a little more expensive at the start, and early repayment may cost a fee.
strings.lx_yourWvar: This is the yearly rate until the next reset. At each reset it can go up or down, and so can the monthly payment.
